title: docs(sdui): three passages name the PIN as the generator version default, not the record
body:
Fixes #18879

Clause-②: no

PR #18875 retired the generator's record-derived version default. `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs`
now resolves the version in one order — `--objectui-version` when passed, otherwise what the PINNED
objectui commit declares in `packages/core/package.json` (through `check-sdui-manifest.mjs`'s own
exported `readPinnedDeclaredVersion`) — and REFUSES when neither answers. Three passages still
described the retired default as current. This repairs those three, and leaves four others alone
because they are conditional, not broken.

## The card's six sites are not one class, and there is a seventh

I enumerated every site on this tree and classified each. The census phrase the card used
(`gen-sdui-manifest-node`, 30 hits tree-wide) plus two wording sweeps (`REUSE`, `already in the
record` / `already recorded` / `already sitting`) is what the enumeration is taken from.

Class (a) — literally false today, repaired here:

1. `scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` check 4's problem text (was :318-319)
2. `packages/spec/scripts/check-react-blocks-declaration-parity.ts` (was :87-88)
3. `scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` header, check 4's own rationale (was :43-47) — NOT on the
   card's six; see "The seventh site" below

Class (b) — conditional, not broken, deliberately untouched:

4. `scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs:228` (artefact missing) — flagless `Regenerate:` prescription
5. `scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs:275` (sha256 mismatch) — flagless `Regenerate:` prescription
6. `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json:10` — flagless prescription; also held by open PR #18723
7. `packages/spec/scripts/manifest-prescription.ts:81` — flagless prescription, and its own text
   already points the reader at where the exact call is printed

## (a) verbatim, before and after

### 1. check 4's problem text

Before (the false sentence is the REASON CLAUSE for the prescription on the line below it):

```
  describes a registry this pin does not name. The generator REUSES the version already recorded when
  --objectui-version is not passed, which is how a regeneration re-records a new pin under an old version.
  Regenerate against the pin: node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs --objectui-version 9.9.9-what-the-pin-declares
```

After:

```
  describes a registry this pin does not name. The generator reads this version from the PIN, never
  from this record, so a disagreement came from outside that default: a version named explicitly on
  some other run, a hand edit, or a record written before the default was fixed to read the pin.
  Regenerate against the pin: node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs --objectui-version 9.9.9-what-the-pin-declares
```

Both blocks are real output, captured by driving `checkTree` against the fixture shape the script's
own self-test uses (a green tree plus a throwaway objectui whose declared version disagrees with the
record). The prescription line is unchanged.

Why the new sentence is true of today's generator: `gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs:149-168` takes
`--objectui-version` when passed, otherwise calls `readPinnedDeclaredVersion(pin)` and `fail`s on any
status but `resolved`; it never reads `record.objectuiPackagesVersion`. Check 4 only runs when
`pin === record.objectuiSha` (check 3 returns early otherwise), so at this point the record names the
LIVE pin and its version field disagrees with what that pin declares. The three routes the new
sentence lists are the ones that survive: an explicit `--objectui-version` naming another version, a
hand edit, and a record written before that default was fixed.

### 2. the node producer's description in the parity gate header

Before:

```
//   node     `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs` writes the TRACKED repo-root
//            artefact under plain Node — no browser, no objectui build. It
//            enumerates the PUBLISHED `@object-ui/*` packages at the version named
//            in `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json`.
```

After:

```
//   node     `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs` writes the TRACKED repo-root
//            artefact under plain Node — no browser, no objectui build. It
//            enumerates the PUBLISHED `@object-ui/*` packages at the version
//            `--objectui-version` names, else the one the PINNED commit's
//            `packages/core/package.json` declares — and REFUSES when neither
//            answers. `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json` is what that run
//            WRITES, never where it reads the version from.
```

Why the new sentence is true of today's generator: the record is the run's OUTPUT
(`gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs:229-240` writes `nextRecord` with `objectuiPackagesVersion: version`),
never its input. The paragraph forty lines below this one in the same header already says the version
is "read off the pinned commit's `packages/core/package.json`", so the file now agrees with itself.

### 3. the seventh site — the same defect, one grep-phrase away

The card's census missed it because the wording differs: the problem text says "the version already
recorded", the header says "the version already in the record", so the card's own firing control
never sounded on it.

Before:

```
 *      with nothing asking whether V is C's version at all (#18611). The live
 *      way to write that record is the generator's own default —
 *      `--objectui-version` unset makes it REUSE the version already in the
 *      record, so a regeneration after a pin bump keeps the OLD version string
 *      while re-recording the NEW pin, and checks 1-3 stay green throughout.
```

After:

```
 *      with nothing asking whether V is C's version at all (#18611). The
 *      generator's own default does not write such a record — `--objectui-version`
 *      unset reads the version off the PIN and REFUSES when the pin cannot be
 *      read — but an explicit wrong version, a hand edit, or a record written
 *      before that default was fixed still produce one, and checks 1-3 stay
 *      green throughout.
```

Repaired in place rather than filed: same file, same defect class, same gate family, mechanical, and
the correct shape was already pinned by the sibling passage above. A full scan of all 25 open
non-release PRs (file lists read one by one) found no other claim on this file.

## Firing control

`git grep -n 'version already recorded' -- '*.mjs' '*.ts' '*.md'`

- before: 1 hit (`scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs:318`)
- after: 0 hits, exit 1

The instrument is not dead. Two positive controls of the same command shape, run on the same tree
after the edit: `'version already sitting in the record'` answers 1 hit in
`scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs`, and `'Regenerate against the pin'` answers 1 hit in
`scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` — the very file the zero is claimed about, so the grep demonstrably
still reaches it.

## (b) decided, with live readings, and the decision differs from triage

Triage framed `:228` / `:275` as "a gate handing you a command it will itself refuse", and half of its
`p2` audience argument rests on that reading. I agree with the PM's narrowing, and I did not take the
reading off the source: I ran the generator both ways in a scratch root, so nothing in this tree was
written.

The scratch root was made discriminating on purpose — its record was seeded with
`objectuiPackagesVersion: "0.0.0-BOGUS-SCRATCH"`, a version that exists on no registry. Had the
retired default still been live, the run would have tried to install it.

Leg 1 — no resolvable pin (`OBJECTUI_ROOT` pointed at a path with no checkout): exit 1, nothing
written, and the refusal carries its own two remedies:

```
✗ gen-sdui-manifest-node: no --objectui-version, and the pinned commit's declared version could not be read: no objectui checkout at /nonexistent-objectui (no .git there). Set OBJECTUI_ROOT to one that carries the pin.
  ⛔ This script does NOT fall back to the version in scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json: after a pin
  bump that re-records the NEW pin under the OLD version string, and check-sdui-manifest.mjs check 4
  reds exactly that record. Either:
    - point OBJECTUI_ROOT at an objectui checkout carrying 53ded82bf7a4…, or
    - pass --objectui-version {the @object-ui version that pin ships} explicitly.
```

Leg 2 — resolvable pin, full run including the network install: exit 0.

```
→ installing @object-ui/* 17.6.0 into /tmp/sdui-manifest-gen-OcPzor (npm, network)...
→ enumerating the registry (16 modules)...
✓ wrote sdui.manifest.json (57 components, 66910 bytes, sha256 49211fee7792…)
✓ re-recorded scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json at pin 53ded82bf7a4 / @object-ui 17.6.0
  (version from packages/core/package.json at objectui 53ded82bf7a4… (read from /home/user/objectui))
```

It resolved `17.6.0` — the version objectui declares at the pin — over the bogus `0.0.0-BOGUS-SCRATCH`
sitting in the record, and overwrote the record with it. The manifest it produced carries
sha256 `49211fee7792…`, byte-matching the artefact tracked here.

So `:228` and `:275` are not broken. The flagless call they print writes the correct artefact whenever
the pin's declared version is readable, and when it is not, it refuses loudly with the remedy in its
own failure text rather than writing a drifted record. That is the behaviour #18875 was for. They are
conditional, and a conditional prescription that fails loudly and names its own fix is not the shape
this repo files cards about. Sites 6 and 7 in the list above are the same conditional shape; site 7
(`manifest-prescription.ts:81`) even printed itself during this round's gate sweep, intact and
actionable, when `check:react-declaration-parity` ran without `MANIFEST` set.

One consequence worth writing down rather than acting on: because the flagless default now reads the
pin, the flagless call would ALSO repair the check-4 record. The flagged prescription is kept
unchanged anyway — it names the value in the command, which is the self-evidencing form, and this
round is prose only.

## DARK — the gate's verdicts do not move

`scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` run before and after the edit, three arms, both streams captured to
files and compared with `cmp`:

| arm | exit before | exit after | stdout | stderr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| plain (resolves the `../objectui` sibling) | 0 | 0 | identical, 290 bytes | identical, 0 bytes |
| `OBJECTUI_ROOT` unresolvable | 0 | 0 | identical, 496 bytes | identical, 0 bytes |
| `OBJECTUI_ROOT` unresolvable + `--require-objectui` | 1 | 1 | identical, 0 bytes | identical, 295 bytes |

`--self-test` is green and its output is byte-identical before and after: 11 cases, battery floor 11.
The strings this PR edits live on failure paths, so a green tree never prints them — which is exactly
why the verdict bytes do not move.

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, run
one by one with each exit code landed to disk before anything read it, then reconciled with `--ran`
carrying those codes.

```
✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 72 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 70 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (2 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3).
```

The two NOT MEASURED are `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure`. Both exit 3 —
their own `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` code — because they load built output and this worktree has no full
`pnpm build`. Both self-tests passed (93 and 22 cases). Neither can be moved by a comment-only diff;
they are declared to CI.

One gate exits 1 under the derived spelling and 0 under CI's: `check:react-declaration-parity` refuses
when `MANIFEST` is unset, which is a prerequisite, not a red. Run as `lint.yml` runs it —
`MANIFEST="$PWD/sdui.manifest.json" ... --baseline react-declaration-parity.baseline.json --strict` —
it exits 0 with "no new DECLARATION divergence vs accepted baseline".

Derivation stability: the 72-family list came out byte-identical at all three tree states this branch
passed through (`625db0e853`, `0ea26d37e8`, `92eee4dcc5`), so the tool's STALE TREE notice — raised
because a sibling agent's fetch keeps advancing the shared `origin/main` ref — changed nothing about
what is owed here.

## Tests and lint

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 scripts/check-react-blocks-declaration-parity.test.ts scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` — 2 files, 115 tests, all passed. These are the suites that name the two edited scripts. `scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` has no sibling test file in `scripts/`; its `--self-test` is its suite, and it is above.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:scripts-typecheck` — exit 0; this is the program that compiles the edited `packages/spec/scripts/**` file.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` after merging `main` — all 15 generated artifacts up to date.
- Dependency-closure build `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/spec^...' build` is an empty run here: "No projects matched the filters" — `packages/spec` has no workspace dependencies.
- Lint, the whole union, as CI runs it, at `92eee4dcc5`: `eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` over a population of **6855 files** read from eslint's own JSON output — 0 errors, 0 warnings. Narrowed to the two edited files: 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. `eslint.config.mjs:326-328` records that this repo "never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules) for ANY file", so nothing in this diff can move an untouched file's verdict either way.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`, measured rather than assumed:

- No package manifest in the repo declares a `files[]` entry reaching `scripts/` — 76 manifests scanned, 0 hits.
- `packages/spec`'s `files[]` is `dist`, `json-schema`, `liveness`, `prompts`, `llms.txt`, `README.md`, `src/**/*.zod.ts`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `api-surface`, `spec-changes.json`. `scripts/` is not among them.
- Grepping every one of those published paths (plus all 202 `src/**/*.zod.ts`) for two distinctive strings from this diff returns zero hits, exit 1. Positive control, same command shape: `PageComponentSchema` answers from `dist/identity/index.js` and three siblings.
- `scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` is a repo-root script belonging to no package.

Nothing published moves, so the tarballs do not move.

## Read-only fences, re-taken at start of work

- `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json` is held by open PR #18723 (state open, draft, 11 files) — confirmed by reading that PR's file list directly, not inherited. Untouched here. Its own stale-ish prescription is class (b) anyway, so the fence costs this round nothing.
- The same scan confirmed #18723 does NOT hold `check-sdui-manifest.mjs`, `check-react-blocks-declaration-parity.ts` or `gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs`, and no other open PR holds any of them.
- `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs` is this round's source of truth and is untouched.
- No self-test making every printed prescription runnable was added. That is a new gate and it is not on this card.
- No product code under `packages/spec/src/`.

## Acceptance notes

Observed, deliberately not filed:

- The card counts "six" sites; a full sweep finds a seventh, in the same file, repaired here under the bounded in-place rule. Noted so the census phrase is on record: a wording sweep keyed on one spelling ("already recorded") will not find its sibling spelling ("already in the record"). Who would hit it: the next reader of check 4's rationale — the same audience as the problem text, which is why it is repaired rather than noted.
- `docs/releases-maintenance.md:116` / `:279`, `scripts/bump-objectui.sh:11` / `:705` / `:739` and `scripts/build-console.sh:282` / `:297` all print the FLAGGED form and are correct today; `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json:5` and `check-sdui-manifest.mjs:19-21` describe the version as "the version `.objectui-sha` ships", which is more true after #18875 than before. None of them is a site. Carrier: none — nothing here needs changing.
